units.k: "A messenger came to me from my Lord and said: pray in this blessed valley" (Bukhari {1}). The valley of Madinah's old estates and the path to the miqat.
"Actions are but by intentions" (Bukhari {1}). The miqats are boundaries the Prophet ﷺ himself appointed (Bukhari {2}).
"Actions are but by intentions, and every person shall have what they intended." — Bukhari {1}

"All of Arafah is a place of standing" (Muslim {1}, Abu Dawud {2}); the exclusion of the hollow of Uranah comes from Ibn Majah {3} (weak chain) and the Muwatta, and the schools agree on it. The Prophet ﷺ camped at Namirah until the sun declined, then moved into Arafah (Muslim {4}).
"An Umrah in Ramadan is equal to a Hajj" (Bukhari {1}) — and in one narration: "a Hajj with me" (Bukhari {2}, Muslim {3}).
"And when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House with Isma'il…" (Quran {1}).
"Begin with what Allah began with" — Quran {1} mentions Safa first; {2} laps ending at Marwah.
"Between my house and my minbar is a garden from the gardens of Paradise" (Bukhari {1}).
"Between my house and my minbar is a garden from the gardens of Paradise." (Bukhari {1})
"Do it, and there is no harm"
"Do not kill game while you are in ihram" — while "game of the sea" stays lawful. The Prophet ﷺ himself had a tent pitched for him at Namirah on the day of Arafah.
"Do you not know that Islam wipes out what came before it, the Hijrah wipes out what came before it, and ___ wipes out what came before it?"
"Hajj is Arafah" (Tirmidhi {1}) — standing there on the {2}th is the pillar without which there is no Hajj.

"Hajj is Arafah" — no dam replaces it. He leaves ihram by doing the acts of an Umrah (tawaf, sa'i and the cut) and performs the Hajj in another year; this is reported as Umar's (RA) ruling for Companions who arrived on the Day of Sacrifice. The majority add a sacrifice; Hanafis owe none.

"Hajj is Arafah", and tawaf al-ifadah is commanded in the Quran. Most schools also count ihram and sa'i as pillars (for Hanafis ihram is a condition and sa'i a wajib), and Shafi'is add the shave or trim.

"Hajj is Arafah. Whoever comes [to Arafah] on the night of Jam' (the night before the {1}th), before Fajr, has caught the Hajj" (Tirmidhi {2}). He ﷺ stood facing the qibla, hands raised, until the sun set (Nasai {3}, Muslim {4}).
"Hajj is Arafah. Whoever comes on the night of Jam', before Fajr, has caught the Hajj." He stands for a moment, then goes on to Muzdalifah.
"Hajj is Arafah." Being there — on the {1}th, or in the night before Fajr of the {2}th — is the pillar without which there is no Hajj.

"He kept standing there till the sun set… and the disc of the sun had disappeared," then moved calmly to Muzdalifah. Stay inside Arafah until sunset; the schools differ on what is owed by one who leaves early.
"I begin with what Allah began with" (Muslim {1}) — Safa is named first in Quran {2}.
"I sacrificed here, and the whole of Mina is a place of sacrifice" — and "all the passes of Makkah are a place of sacrifice." It must be within the Haram.

"If you are prevented, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals." At Hudaybiyyah the Prophet ﷺ slaughtered his hady and shaved. The schools differ on the details — whether illness counts as being prevented, and what must be made up afterwards — so ask a scholar.
"Indeed Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah" (Quran {1}). The two hills of Hajar's seven runs, now an air-conditioned {2} m gallery inside the mosque.
"Indeed, Safa and Marwah are among the symbols of Allah." — Quran {1}

"Indeed, the first House established for mankind was that at Bakkah — blessed and a guidance for the worlds." (Quran {1}). The Kaaba is the qibla of every prayer you have ever prayed. Ibrahim (AS) and his son Isma'il (AS) raised its foundations, praying: <1>"Our Lord, accept this from us"</1> (Quran {2}). When you stand in the mataf you stand where prophets, companions and centuries of believers have stood before you.
"Iqra — Read!" (Quran {1}) descended in Hira, the cave above Makkah (Bukhari {2}).
"It is a mountain that loves us and we love it"
"Jibril came to me and commanded me to order my companions to raise their voices with the talbiyah." Sisters recite it in a low voice.
"Labbayk Allahumma labbayk" — Here I am, O Allah, here I am!
"Labbayk Allahumma labbayk, labbayk la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wan-ni'mata laka wal-mulk, la sharika lak" — "Here I am, O Allah, here I am…" — the Prophet's ﷺ own wording.
"Learn your rites, for I do not know whether I will perform Hajj after this one." — Abu Dawud {1} (also in Muslim)
"Like these. And beware of going to extremes in religion, for those before you were destroyed by going to extremes."
"No one should depart until the last thing he does is the House" (Ibn Majah {1}) — so the shopping, the packing and the goodbyes come first.
"None of you should depart until his last act is at the House" — this is about…
"O Allah, forgive those who shave their heads" — three times, and once for those who shorten (Bukhari {1}). "…with your heads shaved and [hair] shortened, not fearing" (Quran {2}).
"O Allah, forgive those who shave their heads." He said it three times, and the fourth: "…and those who shorten." — Bukhari {1}
"One Umrah to the next is an expiation for whatever (sins) come between them." — Bukhari {1}
"One prayer in al-Masjid al-Haram is better than one hundred thousand prayers elsewhere." — Ibn Majah {1}
"Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." (Quran {1})
"Perform Umrah in Ramadan, for an Umrah in Ramadan is equal to a Hajj." — Bukhari {1}
"Read the Quran, for it will come as an intercessor for its companions on the Day of Resurrection." — Muslim {1}
"Shaving is not a duty laid on women; only clipping the hair is incumbent on them" (Abu Dawud {1}).
"Take the Maqam of Ibrahim as a place of prayer" (Quran {1}) — the Prophet ﷺ recited this very verse then prayed there (Muslim {2}).
"Tawaf around the House is like prayer, except that you speak in it." — Tirmidhi {1}
"Tawaf around the House is like salah" (Tirmidhi {1}) — it needs wudu. Sa'i does not.
"Tawaf around the House is like salah" (Tirmidhi {1}) — so it needs the purity of salah.

"Tawaf around the House is like salah" (Tirmidhi {1}). Make wudu before you start. If it breaks mid-tawaf, renew it: Hanafis and Shafi'is continue from where they stopped, Malikis and Hanbalis restart the tawaf. Follow your group's scholar.
"The Mosque of the Banner" — by tradition the spot where the Prophet ﷺ planted his standard as he entered Makkah at the Conquest of {1} AH, forgiving the city that had expelled him.
"The accepted Hajj has no reward except Paradise." — Bukhari {1}
"The best dua is the dua of the Day of Arafah, and the best that I and the prophets before me said is…"
"The best of supplication is the supplication of the Day of Arafah, and the best of what I and the prophets before me have said is: la ilaha illallah…" (Tirmidhi {1}).
"The days of Mina are three; whoever hastens in two days there is no sin on him, and whoever delays, there is no sin on him." — Tirmidhi {1} (cf. Quran {2})
"The days of tashreeq are days of eating, drinking and the remembrance of Allah" — the "numbered days" of Quran {1}.
"The delegation of Allah are three: the one who fights in His cause, the one performing Hajj and the one performing Umrah." (Nasai {1})
"The first House established for mankind was that at Bakkah — blessed and a guidance for the worlds." (Quran {1})
"The guests of Allah are three: the warrior, the Hajj pilgrim, and the Umrah pilgrim." — Nasai {1}
"The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent, even if small." — Bukhari {1}. Don't let the Haram version of you fade — hold three habits for {2} days after you return.
"The people were ordered to make the tawaf of the House the last thing — except the menstruating women, who were excused." — Bukhari {1}
"The woman in ihram should not wear a niqab or gloves." The niqab is agreed on; most scholars also forbid gloves, while Hanafis permit them. Her ordinary modest clothing in any colour is her ihram.
"There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than…"
"There is no day on which Allah frees more servants from the Fire than…"
"They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel from every distant pass." — Quran {1}
"This day I have perfected for you your religion" (Quran {1}) was revealed…
"Umrah to Umrah is an expiation for what is between them" (Bukhari {1}). Past journeys stay under More▶After▶My journeys.
"Umrah to Umrah is an expiation for what is between them" (Bukhari {1}). When Allah invites you again, the checklists and countdown are ready — nothing from this journey is deleted.
"Umrah to Umrah is an expiation for what is between them, and the reward of an accepted Hajj (mabrur) is…"
"Umrah to Umrah is an expiation for…"
"We used to wait till the sun declined, then do the rami" (Bukhari {1}; Tirmidhi {2}). Those who cannot may stone at night.

"We used to wait till the sun declined, then do the rami" (Ibn Umar, Bukhari {1}); "on the days after (Nahr) he stoned after the zenith of the sun" (Tirmidhi {2}). He ﷺ stoned the first with seven pebbles saying takbir with each, went forward, faced the qibla and made a long dua; the same at the middle one; and did not stop after Aqabah (Bukhari {3}).
"When you depart from Arafat, remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram" — at Muzdalifah (also called Jam'), where the Prophet ﷺ stood in dua after Fajr until it was very bright.
"When you pour down from Arafat, remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram" (Quran {1}). He ﷺ "made takbir, tahlil and dua" there (Muslim {2}).

"Whenever he was asked about anything done before or after, he said: Do it, and there is no harm." Shafi'is and Hanbalis say nothing is owed; Hanafis require a dam for some changes of order, and Malikis a fidyah for shaving before the stoning and a dam for a tawaf al-ifadah done before it.
"Whoever cannot find one — a fast of three days during Hajj and of seven when you have returned. Those are ten complete." Which days count differs a little by school — ask before the {1}th.
"Whoever comes to this House and does not speak obscenely or act wickedly returns as the day his mother bore him." — Muslim {1}
"Whoever eats seven ___ dates in the morning will not be harmed that day by poison or magic."

"Whoever forgets something of his rites or leaves it out, let him shed blood" (Ibn Abbas). A missed wajib is repaired with a dam; a missed pillar is not — it must be done. Which rites are wajib differs a little between the schools, so learn your group's list.

"Whoever had assumed ihram for Hajj, or for Hajj and Umrah together, did not finish the ihram till the Day of Sacrifice." No cutting until after the stoning on the {1}th. (Hanbalis recommend that one who has no hady with him change his ihram to an Umrah on arrival — he then becomes a Tamattu' pilgrim.)
"Whoever has the hady with him should assume ihram for Hajj along with Umrah, and should not finish the ihram till he finishes both." Qiran also owes a hady.

"Whoever hastens in two days there is no sin on him, and whoever delays, there is no sin on him" (Quran {1}). The Prophet ﷺ himself stayed for the {2}th, remaining in Mina through the days of tashriq (Aishah, Abu Dawud {3}).
"Whoever joins Umrah to Hajj must offer what hady is easy" (Quran {1}) — Tamattu' and Qiran. Ifrad owes none.

"Whoever joins Umrah to Hajj must offer what hady is easy; whoever cannot, fasts three days during Hajj and seven when you return — ten in all" (Quran {1}). The Prophet ﷺ slaughtered at Mina and said "all of Mina is a place of sacrifice" (Abu Dawud {2}).
"Whoever joins Umrah to Hajj must offer what hady is easy; whoever cannot, fasts three days during the Hajj and seven when you return — ten in all" (Quran {1}).
"Whoever performs Hajj for Allah, with no intimacy and no sin, returns…"

"Whoever performs Umrah [during the Hajj months] followed by Hajj [offers] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals… This is for those whose family is not in the area of al-Masjid al-Haram." Qiran counts as joining the two, so it owes a hady too; Ifrad owes none. Who counts as a resident differs a little between the schools.
"Whoever performs tawaf around this House seven times and keeps count of it, it is like freeing a slave." — Tirmidhi {1}
"Zamzam is for whatever it is drunk for" — Ibn Majah {1}

units.of: Brief the children: meeting point · "if lost, find a security guard" · snacks & a comfort item

units.k: "…and the accepted Hajj has no reward except Paradise" (Bukhari {1}). Past journeys stay under More▶After▶My journeys.
"…and the accepted Hajj has no reward except Paradise" (Bukhari {1}). When Allah invites you again, the checklists and countdown are ready — nothing from this journey is deleted.
"…and the people of Makkah from Makkah." The companions who had done Umrah entered ihram for Hajj as they set out for Mina — no trip to a miqat is needed.
"…and whoever delays, there is no sin on him — for the one who fears Allah." — Quran {1}
"…as the day his mother bore him" — free of sins, as if born anew.
"…except the menstruating women, who were excused." Safiyyah (RA) could leave because she had already done tawaf al-ifadah. People who live in Makkah do not owe it either.

"…no sexual relations… during Hajj." Before Arafah it spoils the Hajj in all four schools — the Hajj is still completed and then repeated another year; after Arafah the schools differ. Every other violation is repaired by a fidyah, or by nothing.
"…nothing except Paradise." Mabrur: done sincerely, the Sunnah way, without sin — and a life that changes after it.

"…perform tawaf of the Ka'bah and between Safa and Marwah, then cut short his hair and finish his ihram, and later assume ihram for Hajj." Many scholars advise a trim when the {1}th is near, so there is hair to shave on the Day of Nahr.

"…than these ten days." They asked: "Not even jihad in the path of Allah?" He said: "Not even jihad, except a man who goes out with himself and his wealth and returns with nothing." Your Hajj sits inside the best days of the year.
"…the day of Arafah. He draws near, then praises them before the angels: What do these want?" Bring your dua list — and your family's.
"…the penalty is an equivalent from sacrificial animals to what he killed, as judged by two just men… or an expiation: feeding needy people, or the equivalent of that in fasting."

"…then let them complete their rites, fulfil their vows and circle the Ancient House" (Quran {1}). He ﷺ rode to the House and performed tawaf on the Day of Nahr, then prayed Dhuhr in Makkah (Muslim {2}). Safiyyah (RA) got her period after it, and he said "then she will not delay us" (Bukhari {3}).
"…whoever hastens in two days there is no sin on him." — Quran {1}
'Umar (RA) kissed the Stone saying "I know you are a stone… had I not seen the Prophet ﷺ kiss you I would not" (Bukhari {1}) — pure following, not superstition.

'Uthman (RA) bought this well and made it free for all Muslims after the Prophet ﷺ asked: "Who will buy the well of Rumah and put his bucket with the buckets of the Muslims, for better than it in Paradise?" (Tirmidhi {1}; see also Bukhari {2}). Its endowment still funds charity {3} years later.

units.of: (Nusuk permit) ·

units.k: - Before you leave the camp, tell your supervisor, go with a companion and take your phone. - Note the gate you leave by and a building or landmark you can see from it. - To get back, use the location you saved in your phone's map app. - Miqah cannot show a verified map of Mina's camps. Ask your camp guide how your camp's signs and numbers read before you need them. - If you are lost, show your Nusuk card to security staff, a scout or a Nusuk Care point. The Ministry calls the card the main way to identify you and get you help. Scouts run guidance points for lost pilgrims across Mina and walk them back to their camp.

<1>"Between my house and my minbar is a garden (rawdah) from the gardens of Paradise."</1> (Bukhari {1}). It is the small area marked today by green carpets. Entry requires a free timed permit from the Nusuk app — slots open only a short time ahead and the rules (including how often one person may book) change, so check Nusuk as your dates approach and book as soon as slots open, and pray there with presence, not photos.

<1>"Follow up between Hajj and Umrah, for they remove poverty and sins just as the bellows removes the dross of iron, gold and silver."</1> (Tirmidhi {1}). The money you spend on this journey is never a loss.

<1>"One prayer in this masjid of mine is better than a thousand prayers anywhere else, except al-Masjid al-Haram."</1> (Bukhari {1}). The Prophet ﷺ built this mosque with his own hands. Aim to pray all {2} prayers there if your stay allows — but know the famous "{3} prayers" hadith is graded weak; the {4}× virtue applies to every single prayer regardless.

<1>"One prayer in this masjid of mine is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except al-Masjid al-Haram — and one prayer in al-Masjid al-Haram is better than a hundred thousand prayers elsewhere."</1> (Ibn Majah {1}). One Fajr in the Haram outweighs ~{2} years of prayers. Five daily prayers for a week here is a lifetime of reward — never sleep through a congregation.

<1>"The one who fights in Allah's cause, the Hajj pilgrim and the Umrah pilgrim are the delegation of Allah: He called them and they answered, and they ask of Him and He gives them."</1> (Ibn Majah {1}, graded hasan by al-Albani). Arrive with your dua list ready — you have an audience with the Most Generous Host.

<1>"Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it."</1> (Bukhari {1}). At its foot rest Hamza (RA), the Prophet's ﷺ uncle and the Master of Martyrs, with seventy companions of the Battle of Uhud. Visit after Fajr, give salam, and reflect on what they gave for the deen that reached you.

<1>"Whoever is able to die in Madinah, let him die there, for I will intercede for the one who dies there."</1> (Tirmidhi {1}). And: "None patiently endures the hardship of Madinah except that I will be an intercessor or witness for him on the Day of Resurrection." (Muslim {2}).

<1>"Whoever performs tawaf around this House seven times and keeps count of it is like one who frees a slave."</1> With every step "a sin is erased and a good deed is recorded" (Tirmidhi {1}). And tawaf is worship you can ONLY do here — fill your trip with it.
<1><2>Nusuk</2></1> is the official Saudi pilgrim platform (app + website). You need it for:
<1>After an Umrah alone:</1> scholars differ — some require it, many do not; doing it is the safer course.
<1>After ihram, before tawaf:</1> stay in ihram, wait for purity, then perform ghusl, tawaf and sa'i. If bleeding ends in time, nothing is lost.

<1>After midday: small jamarah→middle→Aqabah, {1} pebbles each, dua after the first two</1> (wajib) — Start with the small pillar (nearest Masjid al-Khayf), then the middle, then the big one towards Makkah — the order matters. One pebble at a time with "Allahu akbar". After the first and the second, step aside, face the qibla and make a long dua with your hands raised; after Aqabah, walk away. Time: from midday until sunset; most scholars allow those who cannot make it to stone during the night until Fajr (the Hanbali school has it done the next day after midday instead). Groups are given slots to avoid the crush — keep to yours.

<1>After midday: small→middle→Aqabah, {1} each, dua after the first two</1> (wajib) — Same sequence, same pace, same dua stops. If you are leaving Mina today, carry your bags to the buses first, then stone, then go — or stone and return for the bags, but watch the time. Pebbles: {2}.
<1>Al-Juhfah (near Rabigh)</1> — from Egypt, Syria & the north-west
<1>Arafah:</1> sitting or lying in the tent, or in the bus inside the boundary, counts in full.

<1>Arrive and check you are inside Arafah</1> (sunnah) — Large signs mark the boundary; Wadi Uranah and part of Masjid Namirah lie outside it. Your camp will be inside — but if you walk, stay within the signs. Rest in the shade until Dhuhr; do not fast today — the Prophet ﷺ drank milk at Arafah in front of the people (Bukhari {1}, {2}).
<1>Ascend Safa, face the Kaaba & make dua</1> — Recite the ayah once on approaching Safa, then praise Allah facing the Kaaba and repeat this dhikr with your own duas three times:

<1>At the miqat you say one of three:</1> <2>Labbayk Allahumma 'Umrah</2> (Tamattu') · <3>Labbayk Allahumma 'Umratan wa Hajjan</3> (Qiran) · <4>Labbayk Allahumma Hajjan</4> (Ifrad). Your group leader knows which one your package follows — the app asks again before the hair is cut.

<1>Back to Mina — sleep there tonight</1> (wajib) — After the Haram, return to your camp and spend the night (most of it) in Mina. Pray the prayers shortened (four rakahs if your school counts you a resident of Makkah — see the {1}th), keep the takbir of tashriq going after each one, and rest — tomorrow's stoning is after midday.
<1>Before flying</1> — tawaf al-wada as the very last act (waived for menstruating sisters).

<1>Before the miqat:</1> enter ihram anyway — ihram does not require purity — and keep up the talbiyah, dhikr and dua. When Aishah (RA) got her period at Sarif, the Prophet ﷺ told her: "Do what all the pilgrims do, except that you do not perform tawaf around the Ka'bah until you are clean" (Bukhari {1}).
<1>Buses</1> — SAPTCO and shuttles connect the cities cheaply.

<1>Cannot afford it?</1> Fast {1} days during the Hajj and {2} when home. Best days: the {3}th–{4}th (Shafi'i) or the {5}th–{6}th (Hanafi / Hanbali — the {7}th is allowed for the one who owes this fast, though a pilgrim with no fast to make up does not fast Arafah, Bukhari {8}). Missed them? Malikis and Hanbalis (and al-Shafi'i's old view) allow the days of tashriq (Bukhari {9}–{10}); Hanafis say the hady is then owed instead, and the relied-upon Shafi'i view is that the three days are made up later.
<1>Cannot go at all?</1> Hajj may be performed on behalf of one permanently unable (Bukhari {1}) — the view of the majority; the Malikis disapprove of it for a living person.
<1>Checked</1> against the source texts on {1} {m1} {2}. Scholar review is still pending.

<1>Clothing:</1> ordinary loose modest dress in any colour is your ihram; no niqab tied on the face and, in the majority view, no gloves (Bukhari {1}; the Hanafis permit them); letting a cloth down from the head when men pass is reported from the women with the Prophet ﷺ (Abu Dawud {2} — weak chain; the practice is accepted by the schools).

<1>Collect {1} small pebbles for tomorrow ({2} or {3} if you want them all now)</1> (sunnah) — Chickpea-sized, from the ground anywhere — Muzdalifah, Mina or the road; there is nothing special about Muzdalifah stones, it is simply convenient. There is no need to wash them (the Prophet ﷺ is not reported to have done so; some scholars recommend it), and do not pick big ones. Keep them in a small pouch: {4} for the {5}th, then {6} a day for the {7}th and {8}th (and the {9}th if you stay).

<1>Cover both shoulders, then pray {1} rakahs behind Maqam Ibrahim</1> — Men: cover both shoulders first. Al-Kafirun in the first rakah, al-Ikhlas in the second. If crowded, pray anywhere in the mosque.
<1>Departing within days?</1> Ask a scholar or your group's alim about the concessions — do not decide alone.

<1>Dhikr and dua at al-Mash'ar al-Haram</1> (sunnah) — Stand facing the qibla after Fajr — by the mosque of al-Mash'ar if you are near it, otherwise where you slept. Takbir, tahlil, hamd, then your duas. This is the last of the great standing places — do not sleep through it.

<1>Dhuhr + Asr together at Dhuhr time, two rakahs each</1> (sunnah) — Pray behind the imam at Namirah if you are there, otherwise in the tent with your group: one adhan, two iqamahs, nothing in between. Then the standing begins. Hanafis combine the two only when praying behind the Hajj imam (otherwise each at its own time), and a pilgrim their school counts as a resident of Makkah ({1}+ days; Shafi'is: {2} full days, not counting arrival and departure, and staying on {3} full days after the Hajj; Hanbalis: if staying on in Makkah more than {4} days after the Hajj) prays four rakahs each — in the relied-upon Shafi'i view such a resident also prays each at its own time, since the combining is tied to travel — ask your group leader.
<1>Dhul-Hulayfah (Abyar Ali)</1> — coming from Madinah (~{1} km from Makkah)
<1>Drink Zamzam water</1> — Drink your fill and make dua — "Zamzam water is for whatever it is drunk for." (Ibn Majah {1})
<1>Each round: touch the Yamani corner if easy, then recite…</1> — Touch the Yamani corner if easy (don't kiss it), and between it and the Black Stone recite:
<1>Each time you reach Marwah or Safa: face the Kaaba & repeat the dhikr</1> — Same praise and dua as on Safa. Sa'i commemorates Hajar's trust in Allah — walk it with reflection.
<1>Ehsan</1>Saudi Arabia's official donation platform — sadaqah without scams

<1>Elderly, unwell, sisters and their carers: you may leave after midnight</1> (sunnah) — If standing in the crowds at dawn is beyond you — age, illness, pregnancy, small children, or you are the one escorting them — leave once the moon has set (on this night between about {1} and {2} am, in the last third of the night; Shafi'is and Hanbalis already allow leaving after midnight) and go to Mina. Leaving Muzdalifah after moonset is agreed for the weak; this is a concession the Prophet ﷺ gave, using it is not a shortcoming, and nothing is owed. The time of the stoning differs: Shafi'is and Hanbalis allow it from after midnight (Asma stoned before Fajr, Bukhari {3}); Hanafis and Malikis hold it is valid only from Fajr. Follow your group's school; if unsure, wait for Fajr — it is valid for everyone.

<1>Finish everything else first — bags packed, shopping done</1> (sunnah) — The farewell tawaf must be your last act in Makkah. Settle the hotel, pack, buy the dates and Zamzam, then go to the Haram. Buying food for the road or waiting for your bus afterwards is fine; a long stay or another errand means repeating it (Hanafis: it still counts, though repeating it is preferred).
<1>Flight before purity with ifadah not done:</1> scholars differ — some permit tawaf with precautions in genuine necessity. Do not decide alone: tell your group leader / ask a scholar early.

<1>Flying?</1> Change into ihram garments before boarding or at a stopover; make your intention when the pilot announces the miqat approach (~{1}–{2} min before Jeddah). Many pilgrims wear ihram from the departure airport to be safe.
<1>Flying?</1> Wear ihram before boarding or at the stopover; pray the {1} rakahs at the airport; make the intention when the pilot announces the miqat.
<1>Footwear:</1> sandals or slides; the ankles should be uncovered.
<1>Forgot it:</1> still near Makkah — go back and do it; far away — the majority say a dam, Malikis nothing. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.
<1>Foundations of Hajj</1>Pillars, wajibs, sunnahs & the three types · {1} questions · {2}% unlocks the next level
<1>Foundations of Umrah</1>What Umrah is and how it flows · {1} questions · {2}% unlocks the next level
<1>Ghusl & grooming</1> — Shower, trim nails, remove unwanted hair. Men may apply perfume to the body (not the garments) before intention.

<1>Ghusl, perfume on the body, ihram garments — from your hotel</1> (sunnah) — Morning of the {1}th (or the night before, if your bus leaves early). Shower, trim nails, men perfume the body not the cloth, put on the izar and rida. Women: ordinary modest clothing. There is no miqat for this ihram — you assume it where you are staying in Makkah, Aziziyah included.

<1>Go to Mina · pray Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha and Fajr there — each at its time, the four-rakah ones shortened</1> (sunnah) — Most groups move by bus (some walk) in the morning or afternoon — the Mashaer train links only Mina, Muzdalifah and Arafah, not Makkah itself; find your camp and maktab number before you do anything else. Four-rakah prayers are prayed as two, each at its own time, in your tent or at Masjid al-Khayf. Shortening is for travellers: Malikis shorten in Mina and Arafah regardless (as do many Saudi scholars today); Hanafis ({1}+ days in Makkah before the {2}th) count you a resident and pray four rakahs here; Shafi'is count you a resident after {3} full days in Makkah (not counting the days of arrival and departure), but let you shorten from the moment you leave for Mina if you will set off for home after the rites without another {4} full days in Makkah (al-Majmu' {5}/{6}); Hanbalis shorten unless you will stay on in Makkah for more than {7} days after the Hajj — ask your group leader which your group follows. Spend the day in talbiyah, Quran and rest — tomorrow is the big day.
<1>Going to Madinah or Jeddah next:</1> do it when you leave Makkah; it is not repeated later.
<1>Hajj rulings:</1> confirm with your group leader or a scholar.
<1>Haramain High-Speed Rail</1> — Jeddah Airport↔Makkah about {1} min; Makkah↔Madinah about {2}¼ hrs (some trains longer). Book online in advance.
<1>Hijr Isma'il</1> — the semicircle was part of the original Kaaba; praying inside it counts as praying inside the Kaaba (Tirmidhi {1}).

<1>How:</1> nearly everyone buys an <2>Adahi</2> voucher (the official platform, usually through the package); the slaughter happens in the Mina abattoirs on your behalf and the meat is distributed — you do not need to attend. Keep the receipt; shave once the time on it has passed.
<1>Idtiba' (men): uncover the right shoulder</1> — Pass the rida under the right arm and over the left shoulder — for this tawaf only.

<1>If your flight comes before purity</1>, the rulings differ (some scholars permit tawaf with precautions in genuine necessity) — ask a scholar you trust before travelling; do not decide alone at the airport.
<1>Ifrad</1> — Hajj alone (<2>Labbayk Allahumma Hajjan</2>): arrival tawaf and sa'i, in ihram until the {1}th. <3>No hady.</3> An Umrah can be done afterwards from Tan'eem.

<1>Izar (lower cloth):</1> hold it behind you at waist height, wrap the left side across the front, then the right side over it; fold the top edge down over itself {1}–{2} times to lock it. Wear a belt or money pouch over the fold — a belt is fine in ihram.

<1>Labbayk Allahumma labbayk</1> — "Here I am, O Allah, here I am." You are answering a call announced by Ibrahim (AS) thousands of years ago: "And proclaim to the people the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel from every distant pass." (Quran {1}). Every phrase strips away shirk: <2>la sharika lak</2> — You have no partner; all praise, all favour, all sovereignty are Yours alone. Say it with meaning, not momentum — men aloud, women softly — in Umrah until you begin the tawaf, in Hajj until you stone Jamrat al-Aqabah on the {2}th.

<1>Leaving today? Be out of Mina before the sun sets — otherwise stay and stone on the {1}th</1> (wajib) — Both choices are from the Quran: leave after today's stoning (nafr al-awwal) or stay the extra night and stone again tomorrow (nafr ath-thani — what the Prophet ﷺ did, and the greater reward). If you choose to leave, your group must be outside Mina's boundary before sunset. If the sun sets while you are still inside — the majority say you now stay the night and stone on the {2}th (Hanafis: only if you are still there at Fajr). Being stuck in a departing bus inside the boundary is, for most scholars, excused.
<1>Life with Allah</1>Daily adhkar & duas from the Sunnah

<1>Madinah ziyarah:</1> the City Sightseeing hop-on hop-off bus ({1} routes, {2}- to {3}-hour tickets) reaches Quba, Qiblatayn and Uhud with commentary (check the current route map) — <2>book it from the Places tab</2>.
<1>Madinah</1>Haramain train · settle · Maghrib & Isha in Masjid an-Nabawi · salam to the Prophet ﷺ
<1>Madinah</1>Last salam to the Prophet ﷺ · depart
<1>Make the intention at the miqat</1> — At the miqat — or, if flying, when the pilot announces it (~{1}–{2} min before Jeddah). The rules of ihram now apply.
<1>Make the intention for Hajj (Ifrad) at the miqat</1> — At the miqat — or, if flying, when the pilot announces it (~{1}–{2} min before Jeddah). The rules of ihram now apply.

<1>Make the intention for Hajj</1> (rukn) — Say it with your heart and tongue before you set off for Mina. From this moment the ihram rules apply again until the {1}th. If you fear illness or an obstacle, add the condition (ishtirat) — see your Umrah ihram step.
<1>Make the intention for Umrah and Hajj together (Qiran) at the miqat</1> — At the miqat — or, if flying, when the pilot announces it (~{1}–{2} min before Jeddah). The rules of ihram now apply.

<1>Make wudu — required for tawaf</1> — Most scholars hold tawaf is not valid without wudu, so make it before you enter. If it breaks mid-tawaf, renew it: the Hanafi and Shafi'i schools let you continue from where you stopped; the Maliki and Hanbali schools say restart the tawaf, which is the safer course. Enter the mosque with the right foot:
<1>Makkah</1>All five prayers in the Haram · nafl tawaf after Fajr · rest
<1>Makkah</1>Arrive · ihram at the miqat (in flight) · Umrah tonight when rested
<1>Makkah</1>Arrive · ihram at the miqat (in flight) · the arrival tawaf (and sa'i if you do it now) when rested — you stay in ihram until the {1}th
<1>Makkah</1>Nafl tawaf · rest — save your strength for the {1}th
<1>Makkah</1>Quran facing the Kaaba · Hijr Isma'il late night · Clock Tower museum
<1>Makkah</1>Tawaf al-wada — the last thing you do · {1} rounds · waived for sisters on their period · then the train to Madinah

<1>Maqam Ibrahim</1> — the stone Ibrahim (AS) stood on while raising the Kaaba's walls (Bukhari {1}); his footprints were preserved in it, and Allah says "Take the Maqam of Ibrahim as a place of prayer" (Quran {2}).

<1>Meanwhile</1>, everything else in Daily still counts: dhikr and dua, Quran by listening or tafsir (the Malikis and many scholars, including Ibn Baz, also allow reciting from memory), sadaqah, serving pilgrims, Zamzam, your dua list.

<1>Men: shave (halq) or trim all around (taqsir) — the first tahallul</1> (wajib) — Shaving is the greater reward. Barbers crowd the Jamarat exits and the Aziziyah streets — use a licensed shop and a fresh blade. After the stoning and the cut (Shafi'is and Hanbalis: any two of stoning, cut and tawaf) you are in the first tahallul: everything is allowed again except intimacy and the marriage contract (Hanafis: intimacy only, since they permit the contract even in ihram; Malikis: and hunting; they also dislike perfume until tawaf al-ifadah, with nothing owed) — shower, normal clothes. Aishah (RA) perfumed the Prophet ﷺ at this point, before his tawaf (Bukhari {1}).
<1>Men: shave (halq) or trim all around (taqsir)</1> — Shaving carries the greater reward. Licensed barbershops cluster around the Marwah exit.

<1>Missed it?</1> Cannot afford a hady? The Quran's own alternative: fast three days during Hajj and seven days when you are home. Best the {1}th–{2}th (Shafi'i) or the {3}th–{4}th (Hanafi / Hanbali — the {5}th is allowed for the one who owes this fast). Missed them? Malikis and Hanbalis allow the days of tashriq (Bukhari {6}–{7}), as does al-Shafi'i's old view; the relied-upon Shafi'i view does not, so the three days are made up later; Hanafis say the hady is then owed instead. Forgot to arrange it? It may be slaughtered until sunset on the {8}th according to Hanafis, Malikis and Hanbalis, or the {9}th according to many contemporary scholars (Shafi'is set no last day, though the {10}th is best); after that most scholars say it is still owed and must be made up. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Changed into normal clothes before cutting? Put the ihram back on if you can and cut now. Whether a fidyah is owed differs: Shafi'is and Hanbalis excuse clothing worn forgetfully or unknowingly, but not cutting hair or nails; Hanafis require it regardless, and so do Malikis unless you had already stoned (for them the stoning alone opens the first tahallul); some Hanbalis and many contemporary scholars say nothing is owed for forgetting or not knowing (Bukhari {1}) — a fast of {2} days, feeding {3} poor, or a sheep (Quran {4}; the amounts are from Bukhari {5}). Shaved before the hady or before the rami? "No harm" (Bukhari {6}) for Shafi'is and Hanbalis; Hanafis: a dam; Malikis: a fidyah for shaving before the rami. Left Makkah without ever cutting? Cut as soon as you remember, wherever you are — until then intimacy stays forbidden. Hanafis and Malikis say a dam is owed; Shafi'is and Hanbalis say nothing is owed for the delay. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.
<1>Missed it?</1> Did an errand afterwards and the bus has not left? Simply do the tawaf again. Already left? See the next step, and tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Did not stay in Muzdalifah at all, or left before midnight without an excuse? The majority say a dam is owed (a sheep, slaughtered and given to the poor of the Haram); the Hajj is valid. Hanafis count the wajib as being there after Fajr, so leaving after midnight without excuse is also a dam for them. Those with a valid excuse (see the next step) owe nothing. Stuck in a bus queue and arrived only after Fajr? Scholars differ; most say nothing is owed if you did your best. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Did them out of order? "No harm" (Bukhari {1}) — Shafi'is and Hanbalis say nothing is owed. Hanafis: a dam for shaving before the stoning, or (Qiran / Tamattu') for sacrificing before the stoning or shaving before the hady; Malikis: a fidyah for shaving before the stoning, and a dam for a tawaf al-ifadah done before it. Mention it to your group leader so the rest of the day is sequenced right, and ask a scholar if your group follows the Hanafi school.

<1>Missed it?</1> Forgot it or left it for later? Do it whenever you remember, even days later — it does not need ihram or a new tawaf, only to come after a tawaf you have already done (Malikis: do the sa'i straight after the tawaf; after a long gap repeat the tawaf first). Never done at all? It is a pillar for the majority (a wajib with a dam for Hanafis), so the Hajj stays incomplete until it is done. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.
<1>Missed it?</1> Forgot the ghusl or the perfume? Nothing is owed — both are sunnah. Just make the intention and carry on. If in doubt, tell your group leader or ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Forgot to cut? Cut now. Your ordinary clothes were never a problem — women wear them in ihram — and the delay itself owes nothing if you cut by the {1}th. If you did something else forbidden before cutting (perfume, cutting nails, niqab or gloves): Shafi'is and Hanbalis excuse perfume used forgetfully but not cutting nails; Hanafis require the fidyah regardless; Malikis owe nothing once you had stoned (the stoning alone opens their first tahallul); many contemporary scholars excuse all forgetting (Bukhari {2}) — a fast of {3} days, feeding {4} poor, or a sheep (Quran {5}; the amounts are from Bukhari {6}). Left Makkah without cutting? Cut as soon as you remember. Hanafis and Malikis say a dam is owed; Shafi'is and Hanbalis say nothing is owed for the delay. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> If you cut your hair or changed into ordinary clothes after the arrival tawaf by mistake, your ihram still stands — put the ihram back on, stop the act, and carry on. Whether a fidyah is owed differs: Shafi'is and Hanbalis excuse perfume and clothing done forgetfully or unknowingly, but not cutting hair or nails; Hanafis and Malikis require the fidyah regardless; some Hanbalis and many contemporary scholars say nothing is owed for anything done forgetfully or unknowingly (Bukhari {1} — a man in a perfumed cloak was simply told to remove it). The fidyah is a fast of {2} days, feeding {3} poor, or a sheep (Quran {4}; the amounts are from the hadith of Ka'b ibn Ujrah, Bukhari {5}). Tell your group leader / ask a scholar whether one applies to you.

<1>Missed it?</1> If you discover you spent the whole day outside the boundary (in Uranah), move inside now — any moment inside Arafah between Dhuhr of the {1}th (Hanbalis: from Fajr of the {2}th) and Fajr of the {3}th makes the wuquf valid (Malikis: it must include a moment after sunset, so stay inside until the sun has set). Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> If you were not inside Arafah at any moment between Dhuhr on the {1}th (Hanbalis: from Fajr of the {2}th) and Fajr on the {3}th, there is no Hajj this year: you exit by doing the rites of Umrah (tawaf, sa'i, cut the hair) and make the Hajj up another year — a hady is owed according to the majority (Hanafis: none), and the Hajj is still obligatory on you. Arrived after sunset but before Fajr? Your wuquf is valid (Tirmidhi {4}). Tell your group leader / ask a scholar before you do anything.

<1>Missed it?</1> Left Makkah without it? If you are still close (Shafi'is and Hanbalis: under about {1} km, the distance for shortening prayers; Hanafis: before passing the miqat), go back and do it — nothing is owed. If you are already far away or home, the majority say a dam is owed (a sheep slaughtered in the Haram, which a trusted person there can arrange); Malikis hold it is a sunnah with nothing owed. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Left without it while pure? If still close, go back and do it; if far away, the majority say a dam is owed (Malikis: nothing). Left while menstruating? Nothing is owed at all. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Missed after midday and left? Stone before sunset if you can get back; after sunset of the {1}th the days of stoning are over and a dam is owed for a day's stoning left undone (for a pebble or two the schools differ). Unable? Delegate (permitted by all four schools — Ibn Majah {2} has a weak chain, its meaning is accepted; Malikis add a dam for the one unable). Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Missed or done before midday? Repeat after midday, or stone tomorrow in order (the {1}th's three, then the {2}th's) — the stoning is made up; Shafi'is and Hanbalis: nothing more is owed, Hanafis and Malikis: a dam for the delay. If the {3}th passes with it undone, a dam is owed by all. Unable? Delegate (permitted by all four schools — Ibn Majah {4} has a weak chain, its meaning is accepted; Malikis add a dam for the one unable). Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Missed today? Stone it tomorrow before that day's three, in order: today's three first, then tomorrow's — the stoning is made up. Shafi'is and Hanbalis: nothing more is owed; Hanafis and Malikis: a dam is owed for the delay. Stoned before midday? The majority count it as not done — repeat it after midday (Hanafis allow before midday only on the {1}th; a few contemporary scholars permit it on the {2}th for the weak in severe crowding — ask before relying on it). Unable to go? Delegate to someone who has stoned for themselves (permitted by all four schools — Ibn Majah {3} has a weak chain, its meaning is accepted; Malikis add a dam for the one unable). If the {4}th passes with any day undone, a dam is owed by all. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Missed with no excuse? For a single night the schools differ: the Malikis owe a dam, as do the Hanbalis in their relied-upon view (another Hanbali view: a mudd of food), the Shafi'is a mudd of food, the Hanafis nothing (they count the nights as sunnah); missing all the nights owes a dam for the majority. Valid excuses remove it. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Missed with no excuse? For this night alone the schools differ: the Malikis owe a dam, as do the Hanbalis in their relied-upon view (another Hanbali view: a mudd of food), the Shafi'is a mudd of food, the Hanafis nothing; missing all the nights owes a dam for the majority — see the night of the {1}th. Excuses (illness, caring, no space) remove it. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Never done? The Hajj is not complete: intimacy stays forbidden until you do it — even if that means months later or a return trip; nothing else substitutes for it. Delayed past the {1}th? Valid, and most scholars say nothing is owed (Hanafis: a dam once sunset on the {2}th has passed, unless a period caused the delay; Malikis: a dam once Dhul Hijjah ends). A sister whose period will not end before the group leaves: scholars differ — some permit tawaf with precautions in genuine necessity; do not decide alone. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> No pebbles? Pick them up anywhere in Mina on your way to the Jamarat — the ground around the camps is full of them. Nothing is owed. If in doubt, tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Not stoned today? Do it tonight (most scholars; the Hanbali school: tomorrow after midday) or, at the latest, tomorrow before that day's three jamarat (today's first, in order) — the stoning is made up. Shafi'is and Hanbalis: nothing more is owed; Hanafis: nothing if you stone before Fajr of the {1}th, a dam if it waits until the next day; Malikis: a dam is owed for the delay. If the {2}th passes with it undone, a dam is owed by all. Unable to go at all (illness, age, pregnancy, fear of the crush)? Appoint someone who has stoned for themselves to throw your seven — delegation for the one unable is permitted by all four schools (al-Mughni; the companions stoned on behalf of the children, Ibn Majah {3} — weak chain, meaning accepted); Malikis add that the one unable still owes a dam. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Not yet in ihram and already in Mina or Arafah? Make the intention now, wherever you are — the Hajj is valid as long as you are in ihram before your standing at Arafah ends; whether a dam is owed for assuming it outside Makkah differs between the schools (the Hanbali school: none; others require one, some only outside the Haram boundary, which Mina is inside). If Fajr of the {1}th comes and you never entered ihram, there is no Hajj this year. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.
<1>Missed it?</1> Nothing to make up — a Mufrid owes no hady. If a package insists you pay for one, tell your group leader / ask a scholar.
<1>Missed it?</1> Nothing to make up — this is a permission, not a duty. If you are unsure whether your excuse counts, tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Prayed Maghrib at Arafah or on the bus? For the majority the prayer is valid — combining here is the sunnah, not a condition of Hajj — and nothing is owed. Hanafis say a Maghrib prayed before Muzdalifah must be prayed again there before Fajr, so if your group is Hanafi, repeat it on arrival. Tell your group leader if you are unsure.

<1>Missed it?</1> Prayed them separately or at Asr time? Both prayers are valid; combining is the sunnah, not an obligation. Nothing is owed. Tell your group leader if you are unsure what the group is doing next.

<1>Missed it?</1> Spent the night in Makkah or Aziziyah with no excuse? Most scholars say a dam is owed if the nights are missed (some say one dam for all the nights; Hanafis treat the nights as sunnah with no dam). Illness, caring for the sick, or no space in the camp are valid excuses. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Still in Arafah? Stay until the disc has gone — then nothing is owed. Left before sunset? Hanafis, Shafi'is and Hanbalis: the Hajj is valid. Hanafis and Hanbalis: a dam (a sheep, distributed in the Haram) is owed — Hanafis: returning before sunset removes it; Hanbalis: returning any time before Fajr removes it. Shafi'is (their sounder view): staying until sunset is only recommended, so the dam is recommended, not owed. Malikis: being inside Arafah for part of the night after sunset is a pillar — go back before Fajr or the Hajj is missed. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Sun set while you were still in the camp with your bags, and you left anyway without stoning on the {1}th? The majority say a dam is owed; some scholars excuse those who had already begun to leave and were only held up. Still in Mina now? Simply stay — the {2}th's stoning is after midday tomorrow. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

<1>Missed it?</1> Your package took you straight to Arafah, or you reached Mina only at night? Nothing is owed — the day and night in Mina are sunnah, not a pillar. Rest, keep up the talbiyah, and be in Arafah tomorrow. If in doubt, tell your group leader / ask a scholar.
<1>Multazam</1> — the wall between the Black Stone and the door, where dua is beloved.

<1>Muzdalifah:</1> leave after midnight / moonset with your carer — the Prophet ﷺ sent the weak of his family ahead (Bukhari {1}); nothing is owed. The time of the stoning that follows differs: Shafi'is and Hanbalis allow it from after midnight (Asma stoned before Fajr, Bukhari {2}); Hanafis and Malikis hold it is valid only from Fajr. Follow your group's school; if unsure, wait for Fajr — that is valid for everyone.
<1>Nights in Mina:</1> the sick and their carers are excused (the Prophet ﷺ excused those with a duty elsewhere — Bukhari {1}).

<1>No hady is owed for Ifrad</1> (sunnah) — You carry no sacrifice debt. If you wish, an Adahi voucher as an udhiyah earns the reward of Eid (Hanafis: obligatory if you count as resident — {1}+ days in Makkah — and have the means).
<1>No raml</1> (brisk walk) in the first three rounds of tawaf, and <2>no jogging</2> between the green lights in sa'i — walk at a normal pace throughout. Both are sunnah for men only.

<1>Numbering.</1> Hadith numbers follow sunnah.com; Sahih Muslim is numbered as in the Abdul Baqi edition. The Quran is cited as surah:ayah. A grade is shown only where the app states one. Reports the app cites without a number (such as the Muwatta) are not listed here.
<1>Nusuk Umrah packages</1>Book visas & packages from ministry-licensed providers only
<1>Nusuk</1>Official Saudi platform — visas, Rawdah permits & bookings

<1>On Hajj:</1> a Qiran or Ifrad pilgrim stays in ihram until the {1}th, so any extra Umrah comes after the Hajj, as Aishah (RA) did from Tan'eem (Bukhari {2}). A Tamattu' pilgrim is out of ihram before the {3}th; whether to add Umrahs then is weighed differently by the scholars — many advise saving your strength for the Hajj.

<1>On Hajj:</1> everything continues except tawaf (and the sa'i after it); tawaf al-ifadah waits, and the farewell tawaf is waived if you are still bleeding when you leave — on a Hajj journey, see "Hajj for sisters" in the fiqh Q&A.

<1>On arrival: Maghrib ({1}) + Isha ({2}) together, then nothing else</1> (sunnah) — Muzdalifah is wide ("all of Muzdalifah is a place of standing" — Abu Dawud {3}), but check the boundary signs where your bus stops; the valley of Muhassir is outside it. Pray as soon as you arrive — Maghrib in full, Isha shortened (four rakahs if your school counts you a resident of Makkah — see the {4}th; in the relied-upon Shafi'i view such a resident also prays the two each at its own time), no nafl after. If you fear you will arrive only after midnight, many scholars (including the Saudi fatwa bodies) say pray both on the way before midnight; the four schools still count Isha as on time until Fajr when there is a need. Never let Fajr come without praying them.

<1>Owed by:</1> Tamattu' and Qiran pilgrims — a sheep, or a seventh of a camel or cow (the majority; Malikis do not share a hady, so a whole sheep is valid for everyone). <2>Not owed by:</2> Ifrad pilgrims, nor the residents of Makkah.
<1>Period at Arafah, Muzdalifah or the stoning:</1> nothing changes — none of these requires purity. Aishah (RA) was told: "do what the pilgrims do, except tawaf" (Bukhari {1}).

<1>Period before tawaf al-ifadah:</1> wait. Stay in the first tahallul, keep up the dhikr, and do ghusl, tawaf and sa'i when you are pure — even after the {1}th. The Hajj is complete and nothing is owed (Bukhari {2}).
<1>Period before tawaf al-wada:</1> it is waived — "except the menstruating women, who were excused" (Bukhari {1}); leave with dua from outside the prayer hall.

<1>Pillars</1> (no Hajj without them): ihram, standing at Arafah, tawaf al-ifadah, sa'i (by the majority). <2>Wajibs</2> (by the majority; a dam if missed without excuse): ihram from the miqat, Arafah until sunset, the night at Muzdalifah, the nights of Mina, the stoning, the shave or trim, the farewell tawaf. The schools differ on several: for the Malikis being at Arafah for part of the night is itself a pillar; for the Shafi'is staying until sunset is sunnah and the shave or trim is a pillar; the Hanafis count the nights of Mina as sunnah and sa'i as a wajib; the Malikis count the farewell tawaf as sunnah. Everything else is sunnah for the Shafi'is and Hanbalis — it beautifies the Hajj but costs nothing if missed; the Hanafis and Malikis add duties of their own, some with a dam (e.g. Hanafis: the order of the {1}th's stoning, sacrifice and shave; Malikis: the arrival tawaf of Qiran and Ifrad, unless excused), so ask your group leader.

<1>Practise at home</1> until you can walk, sit and use the bathroom confidently — the number one first-timer anxiety. Safety pins on the izar are used by many pilgrims; scholars differ, so a belt is the cleanest option.
<1>Pray {1} rakahs (if possible)</1> — Recommended before ihram — an obligatory prayer, or {2} rakahs of wudu.

<1>Prayers:</1> sit when you must; combine where the sunnah combines (Arafah, Muzdalifah); shorten in Mina if your school counts you a traveller (Hanafis after {1}+ days in Makkah pray four; so do Shafi'is after {2} full days there, not counting the days of arrival and departure, if they will also stay on {3} full days after the Hajj, and Hanbalis if they will stay on in Makkah more than {4} days after the Hajj — ask your group leader).

<1>Qiran</1> — one ihram for both (<2>Labbayk Allahumma 'Umratan wa Hajjan</2>): arrival tawaf and sa'i, then you stay in ihram until the {1}th — what the Prophet ﷺ himself did because he had his hady with him (Bukhari {2}). <3>Hady owed.</3> The majority: one sa'i covers both; Hanafis: a Qarin does two.

<1>Recite the talbiyah abundantly</1> (sunnah) — Men aloud, women softly — in the bus, in the tent, on the walk. It only stops on the {1}th at Jamrat al-Aqabah: most scholars say at the first pebble; others continue to the last. Either is fine (Malikis stop it on arriving at Arafah after midday on the {2}th).

<1>Rida (upper cloth):</1> drape it over both shoulders like a shawl, covering the back and chest; ends hang in front. For the arrival tawaf, pass it under the right arm (idtiba') (Hanafis and Shafi'is: also in a later tawaf followed by sa'i) — then cover both shoulders again before praying.

<1>Signs:</1> body temperature of {1}°C or more; hot, red skin that may be dry or still sweaty; fast heartbeat and fast breathing; confusion, odd behaviour, or seeing and hearing things that are not there; a seizure; collapse or loss of consciousness.
<1>Signs:</1> headache; dizziness or fainting; heavy sweating with pale, clammy skin; nausea or vomiting; cramps; tiredness or weakness; intense thirst.

<1>Sisters: tawaf al-wada if you are pure — waived if you are on your period</1> (wajib) — If you are pure: {1} rounds in ordinary clothes, no sa'i, then leave as your last act. If your period (or postnatal bleeding) has started and you have already done tawaf al-ifadah: you owe nothing and may leave straight away — say your goodbyes to the House with dua from the courtyard or the gate, without entering the prayer hall. If you have NOT yet done tawaf al-ifadah, that is a different matter — see its step.

<1>Sisters: trim a fingertip's length — the first tahallul</1> (wajib) — Gather the hair and cut about {1} cm from the ends, somewhere private — in the tent, the ladies' area or the hotel. A husband or mahram may cut it for you once he has exited his own ihram. From now on everything is allowed except intimacy and the marriage contract (Hanafis: intimacy only, since they permit the contract even in ihram; Malikis: and hunting; they also dislike perfume until tawaf al-ifadah).
<1>Sleep in Mina tonight</1> (wajib) — Most of the night in the camp. If you went to the Haram for tawaf al-ifadah today, come back before you sleep.

<1>Sleep in Mina · leave for Arafah after sunrise</1> (sunnah) — Drink water, charge your phone, put tomorrow's essentials (ihram spare, umbrella, dua list) in your day-bag. Go to bed early. In the morning, after Fajr and sunrise, move to Arafah with your group saying the talbiyah and the takbir.

<1>Spend the night here · Fajr early · dhikr until the sky brightens · leave before sunrise</1> (wajib) — Sleep on the ground under the sky — the Prophet ﷺ rested rather than staying up in night prayer (many scholars still advise not leaving the witr). Pray Fajr at its first moment, then face the qibla and make dhikr and dua until it is light. Leave for Mina before the sun rises, with the talbiyah.

<1>Stand at Arafah — from Dhuhr until sunset</1> (rukn) — This is the Hajj. Face the qibla, raise your hands and talk to your Lord: istighfar, dua for yourself, your parents, your list, the ummah. Sitting, lying down, in a wheelchair or a bus, inside the tent — it all counts; there is no need to climb Jabal ar-Rahmah. Menstruating sisters stand like everyone else — purity is not required. Pace yourself: water, shade, a little Quran, then dua again.
<1>Start at the Black Stone corner</1> — Face the Stone, raise your hand and say "Bismillahi wallahu akbar". Kiss or touch it only if easy — never push.

<1>Stay until the sun has set, then leave calmly for Muzdalifah</1> (wajib) — Do not join the rush before sunset. When the disc has gone, follow your group to the buses or walk — the path is marked. Maghrib is not prayed on the road: when asked, the Prophet ﷺ said "the prayer is ahead of you" (Bukhari {1}). Keep the talbiyah going.

<1>Stone Jamrat al-Aqabah only — {1} pebbles, takbir with each</1> (wajib) — Walk from Muzdalifah or your Mina camp to the big pillar (the one nearest Makkah, on the level of the bridge your group is assigned). One pebble at a time — never a handful — each with "Allahu akbar"; it must land inside the basin. Stop the talbiyah at the first pebble. Do not stop for dua here. Time: from sunrise until sunset; most scholars allow those who could not make it to stone at night (the Hanbali school has it done the next day after midday instead). The weak who left Muzdalifah early: Shafi'is and Hanbalis allow the stoning from after midnight (Bukhari {2}), Hanafis and Malikis only from Fajr — if unsure, wait for Fajr, which is valid for everyone. Too frail or in a wheelchair? Delegate it — see "Missed it?".

<1>Stoning:</1> go at night when the bridge is quieter (most scholars allow it for those who could not go earlier; the Hanbali school: the next day after midday), or <2>delegate</2> it to someone who has stoned for themselves (permitted by all four schools, al-Mughni — Ibn Majah {1} has a weak chain, its meaning is accepted; Malikis add a dam for the one unable).

<1>Takbir after every prayer · Quran · rest · dua</1> (sunnah) — Pray shortened in the camp or at Masjid al-Khayf — the Prophet ﷺ prayed two rakahs in Mina (Bukhari {1}); four rakahs if your school counts you a resident of Makkah (see the {2}th) — say the takbir after each prayer, drink, eat well and sleep: your body is carrying you through five days of worship. Visit Masjid al-Khayf if it is near; call home.

<1>Tamattu' with a period on arrival</1> (the Umrah tawaf cannot be done before the {1}th): do what Aishah (RA) did — raise the intention to Hajj (Bukhari {2}). For the majority you are then a Qarin, as the Prophet ﷺ told her: "Your tawaf suffices for your Hajj and your Umrah" (Muslim {3}); the hady stays owed, and an Umrah from Tan'eem afterwards is yours if you wish. The Hanafis read "leave the Umrah" as setting it aside, to be made up afterwards — ask your group leader.

<1>Tamattu'</1> — ihram for Umrah at the miqat (<2>Labbayk Allahumma 'Umrah</2>), finish it, live normally in Makkah, then ihram again for Hajj on the {1}th. The Prophet ﷺ ordered his companions without a sacrificial animal to do this (Bukhari {2}) and said he would have done it himself had he not brought his hady (Bukhari {3}). <3>Hady owed.</3> The choice of almost every package, and this app's default.
<1>Tarteel AI</1>AI Quran recitation — mistake detection & memorisation

<1>Tawaf & sa'i:</1> a wheelchair, the electric carts and the upper floors are fully valid (Bukhari {1}); wheelchairs are available free or for rent at official points around the Haram (ask the Haram staff) — never pay touts.

<1>Tawaf al-ifadah — {1} rounds, with wudu, no raml, no idtiba'</1> (rukn) — The pillar that completes your Hajj. Go to the Haram (today is the sunnah; any day of tashriq is fine — Hanafis: by sunset on the {2}th — and later is still valid). Same {3} rounds as your Umrah tawaf, but in ordinary clothes and without the brisk walk (Hanafis and Shafi'is: raml in the first three if a sa'i follows) — then two rakahs and Zamzam. Open the counter — it will not touch your Umrah record. <2>Sisters on their period:</2> wait until you are pure, then do ghusl, tawaf and sa'i; your Hajj is intact and you remain in the first tahallul meanwhile. If your flight comes first, see "Missed it?".

<1>Tawaf al-wada — {1} rounds in ordinary clothes, then leave</1> (wajib) — With wudu, {2} rounds, no raml, no idtiba', no sa'i; two rakahs after it if you can, a last drink of Zamzam, a last dua at the door — and go. If you leave tawaf al-ifadah to the day you depart, it counts as the farewell tawaf too for the Malikis and Hanbalis (and Ibn Baz and Ibn Uthaymin); the Shafi'is still require a separate farewell tawaf — ask your group leader. Not required if you live in Makkah. Going to Madinah next? Do it when you leave Makkah, not after Madinah. Jeddah counts as leaving.
<1>Taxis / Uber / Careem</1> — plentiful; agree street-taxi fares before riding.
<1>The Yamani corner</1> — touched (not kissed) each round when possible.

<1>The dua of Arafah</1> (sunnah) — Say it slowly, again and again, with your own duas between. These hours of Arafah are among the most precious of the whole year — "there is no day on which Allah frees more people from the Fire than the Day of Arafah" (Sahih Muslim).

<1>The hady — your sacrifice</1> (wajib) — A Qarin owes a hady exactly like a Mutamatti' (Quran {1} covers both by the majority view). Nearly every pilgrim pays it as an Adahi voucher through the package or the official Adahi platform; it is slaughtered on your behalf in Mina on the {2}th or the days of tashriq — you do not need to be there. Keep the receipt. Once your time slot has passed, you may shave.

<1>The hady — your sacrifice</1> (wajib) — Nearly every pilgrim pays it as an Adahi voucher through the package or the official Adahi platform; it is slaughtered on your behalf in Mina on the {1}th or during the days of tashriq — you do not need to be there. Keep the receipt. Once your time slot has passed (or the voucher says so), you may shave. Buying a sheep yourself and attending is a beautiful sunnah if your group arranges it.

<1>The sa'i of Hajj — only if you have not already done it</1> (rukn) — If you did sa'i after your arrival tawaf, nothing more is needed and you are now in the second tahallul. If you did not, do it now, straight after tawaf al-ifadah: Safa dhikr, {1} laps, finish on Marwah.

<1>The sa'i of Hajj — only if you have not already done it</1> (rukn) — If you did sa'i after your arrival tawaf, you are done — one sa'i covers both for a Qarin by the majority view, and you are now in the second tahallul. If you did not, do it now after tawaf al-ifadah. Hanafis hold that a Qarin performs two sa'is (one for Umrah, one for Hajj): if you follow that school or your group leader says so, do the second one — an extra sa'i never harms.

<1>The sa'i of Hajj — {1} laps, Safa to Marwah</1> (rukn) — Your Umrah sa'i was for the Umrah; this one is for the Hajj. Straight after tawaf al-ifadah, in ordinary clothes: the same Safa dhikr, {2} laps, finish on Marwah. Use the sa'i counter. With tawaf and sa'i done you are in the second tahallul — everything is allowed.

<1>The sunnah order: rami→hady→halq→tawaf al-ifadah</1> (sunnah) — Follow it if you can. If the group's schedule or the crowds change the order, nothing is lost — the Prophet ﷺ was asked about every variation that day and answered "no harm".

<1>Too ill to continue?</1> With the conditional intention (ishtirat) made at the miqat, the Shafi'is and Hanbalis hold you leave ihram with nothing owed (Bukhari {1}); the Hanafis and Malikis do not give the condition this effect. Without it, the schools differ — the Hanafis treat illness as being prevented, so the hady of Quran {2} applies, while the majority say you stay in ihram until you can complete the rites — ask a scholar through your group leader.
<1>Wear ihram garments</1> — Men: two unstitched white cloths (izar & rida), sandals. Women: ordinary modest clothing.

<1>What to do:</1> call {1} first (or {2}, the Saudi Red Crescent). Then cool the person hard while you wait: move them to shade or air conditioning, remove outer clothing, pour or spray cool water over them, especially the head and neck, and fan them; put ice or cold packs on the neck and armpits if you have them. Do not try to make someone drink if they are confused, drowsy or unconscious. If they become unconscious, lay them on their side in the recovery position and check their breathing; start CPR if there is no sign of life.

<1>What to do:</1> get into shade or air conditioning. Loosen or remove extra clothing. Spray or sponge the skin with cool water, especially the head and neck, and fan it; cold packs wrapped in cloth on the neck or armpits help. Drink cold water, or oral rehydration salts mixed with water.

<1>What:</1> seven rounds in ordinary clothes, with wudu, no raml, no sa'i; two rakahs after it (sunnah for the Shafi'is and Hanbalis; wajib for the Hanafis and many Malikis); then leave. "No one should depart until the last thing he does is the House" (Ibn Majah {1}; Bukhari {2}).

<1>When men pass close by:</1> Aishah (RA) reported that the women with the Prophet ﷺ in ihram would let their outer garment down from the head over the face while riders passed, then uncover again (Abu Dawud {1}, which al-Albani and others grade weak; a similar practice is reported with a sound chain from women in ihram with Asma bint Abi Bakr, Muwatta Malik). Scholars differ on how far this applies today — many allow a loose cloth draped from the head that does not sit tied on the face; others say the face stays uncovered. Follow the scholar you trust; either way, a tied niqab is not worn in ihram.

<1>When:</1> as the last act — pack and shop first. Buying provisions for the road, waiting for the bus, or joining a prayer whose iqamah is called afterwards does not spoil it; a long stay or trading does, and it is repeated (Hanafis: it still counts, though Abu Hanifa preferred repeating it).

<1>When:</1> the {1}th after stoning is the sunnah. The Hanafis, Malikis and the Hanbali school allow it until sunset on the {2}th; some Hanbalis and many later scholars allow the {3}th too, and the Shafi'is set no last day — the {4}th–{5}th is valid for everyone. "All of Mina is a place of sacrifice" (Abu Dawud {6}).

<1>Which?</1> Arriving days before the {1}th: Tamattu' — easier on the body and the family, and what the Prophet ﷺ wished for himself. Arriving on the {2}th or {3}th straight into the rites: Qiran or Ifrad spare you a second ihram. Whatever you said at the miqat is what you are — the app asks you at the halq step of your Umrah.
<1>Who:</1> everyone leaving Makkah after Hajj — wajib for the majority, sunnah for the Malikis. Not the residents of Makkah; not menstruating or postnatal sisters (Bukhari {1}).

<1>With children:</1> stay inside the tent during the midday heat · the standing is valid sitting, lying down or asleep · let them hold your hand while you make dua · leave for the buses only when the group leader says.

<1>With children:</1> use the upper floor or a pre-Fajr slot · keep the child close beside you, holding hands, and stay well away from the Kaaba wall · pushchairs and wheelchairs take the middle lanes of the Mas'a · agree a numbered-gate meeting point · let an older child tap the counter.

<1>Women: trim a fingertip's length</1> — Gather the hair and cut about {1} cm from the ends — never shave.

A <1>dam</1> ("blood") is a sheep — or, for the majority, a seventh of a camel or cow — slaughtered in the Haram and given to its poor, which makes up for a <2>wajib</2> left out: leaving Arafah before sunset, missing the night at Muzdalifah or the nights of Mina without excuse, a day of stoning still undone after the {1}th, leaving without the shave or trim, or the farewell tawaf for one who has already gone far. The basis is the ruling of Ibn Abbas (RA): "whoever leaves out a rite, or forgets it, let him shed blood" — a companion's statement reported in the Muwatta, not a hadith of the Prophet ﷺ. Your <3>Hajj remains valid</3>; the dam repairs it. A <4>pillar</4> is different: Arafah missed means the Hajj is missed; tawaf al-ifadah — and, for the majority, sa'i — cannot be replaced by a dam; they must simply be done, however late (the Hanafis count sa'i as a wajib that a dam repairs). Scholars differ on details (Hanafis treat the nights of Mina as sunnah; Malikis treat the farewell tawaf as sunnah; for the Malikis, leaving Arafah before sunset without returning that night means the Hajj is missed, while for the Shafi'is staying until sunset is only sunnah; the Shafi'is count the shave or trim as a pillar that must be done, not repaired by a dam), and nothing is owed for a valid excuse in most cases. Arrange a dam through your group leader or a trusted service in Makkah — never a street tout — and ask a scholar which applies to you.
A <1>dam</1> for a missed wajib is a separate sheep — see the fiqh Q&A.

This is not a hadith of the Prophet ﷺ: it is the takbir that the Companion Ibn Mas'ud (RA) said in the days of tashriq, recorded by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf with a chain its editor grades sahih. No single wording is fixed from the Prophet ﷺ, so there is room: the Hanafis prefer this form, al-Shafi'i preferred starting with three takbirs, and Ibn Abbas (RA) used another wording.

A full Umrah (seven circuits of tawaf and seven laps of sa'i) is a long walk on an empty stomach, and Makkah is warm in {H1} {1} (February to early {M1} {2}): long-term average daytime highs are about {3}°C in February and {4}°C in March. Consider doing your Umrah after iftar, once you have eaten and drunk. The Ministry of Health advises drinking at least {5} cups of water spread between iftar and suhoor, not all at once at suhoor, limiting tea and coffee, and keeping out of the sun in the daytime. If you feel dizzy or confused or cannot stand, drink water at once, ideally an oral rehydration solution, as the Ministry advises: the sick are excused from fasting and make the day up later (Quran {6}). In the last ten nights the prayers run late, so plan to rest after Fajr or in the afternoon.

A hand-held umbrella: allowed by most scholars (the Hanafis, the Shafi'is, one narration from Imam Ahmad, and some Maliki authorities such as Khalil). When the Prophet ﷺ stoned Jamrat al-Aqabah, Usamah and Bilal (RA) were with him: one led his camel and the other held up a cloth over his head to shade him from the heat (Muslim {1}). Some jurists disliked or forbade it, but there is no consensus against it.

A light umbrella. A refillable water bottle. Oral rehydration sachets. Sunglasses. A small spray bottle for water. Loose, light-coloured clothing (sisters) and a spare ihram (brothers). Your usual medicines, with a written list of them and their doses. The numbers {1}, {2} and {3} saved in your phone and written on paper.

A long, long time ago, when only a few families lived in Makkah around the well of Zamzam, Allah told Prophet Ibrahim to build a special House — a House just for worshipping Allah. Ibrahim was old, but his son Isma'il was young and strong. Isma'il carried the stones and Ibrahim stacked them up, wall by wall. When the walls grew too high to reach, Ibrahim stood on a stone — you can still see that stone today; it is called Maqam Ibrahim. While they worked they kept praying: "Our Lord, accept this from us!" They did not build it for a king. They built it for Allah. That is the Kaaba — the very first House built for people to worship Allah. Every Muslim in the whole world faces it when they pray — and now you are standing right in front of it!

Aishah (RA) perfumed him "for his release, when he came out of ihram, before he performed tawaf" — that is, before tawaf al-ifadah. Clothes, nails and perfume return at this first release; intimacy waits for tawaf al-ifadah — and, for most schools, the sa'i too if you still owe it. Aishah (RA): "Some of us assumed ihram for Umrah only, some for both Hajj and Umrah, and others for Hajj only" (Bukhari {1}). All three are valid; the difference is how Umrah and Hajj are joined.
Aishah (RA): Quraysh (al-Hums) stayed at Muzdalifah while the other Arabs stood at Arafah; with Islam, Allah ordered His Prophet ﷺ to go to Arafah, stand there and depart from there.

Aishah (RA): those who had assumed ihram for Umrah "performed tawaf round the Kaaba and between Safa and Marwah, then finished their ihram; after returning from Mina they performed another tawaf [between Safa and Marwah]. Those who had combined Hajj and Umrah performed only one" (Bukhari {1}). Tamattu' = two sa'is; Qiran and Ifrad = one (Hanafis: two for a Qarin).

Aishah (RA): those who had done Umrah first "performed another tawaf (between Safa and Marwah) after returning from Mina." The four schools require this second sa'i of the Tamattu' pilgrim, normally after tawaf al-ifadah; a minority (e.g. Ibn Taymiyyah) held the first sa'i suffices.

Aishah asked the Prophet ﷺ what she should say if she knew which night was Laylat al-Qadr. He said: "Say: O Allah, You are Pardoning and You love to pardon, so pardon me." (Ibn Majah {1} and Tirmidhi {2}. Al-Tirmidhi called it hasan sahih and al-Albani graded it sahih, though some graders weaken its chain.) Many printed copies of al-Tirmidhi add the word "karim" (Generous); al-Albani found it in none of the early sources and judged it a copyists' addition, so the shorter wording is given here.

Around the Haramain you will meet rehearsed stories: a mother with a sleeping baby (sometimes rented for the day), "my wallet was stolen and I need a ticket home", "my child needs surgery", a shown photo of a sick relative. Organised gangs run many of these, and they target pilgrims whose hearts are soft after worship. <1>Your mercy is not naive — but your money should be smart:</1> give through Ehsan, your trusted charity at home, or to people whose situation you actually know. Begging is illegal in the Haramain; report persistent cases to security rather than engaging.

At Arafah the Prophet ﷺ prayed Dhuhr and then Asr, both at the time of Dhuhr, with one adhan and two iqamahs and nothing in between (Jabir, Muslim {1}), each shortened to two rakahs. Salim told al-Hajjaj that the sunnah is to pray early, just after midday, that day, and Ibn Umar (RA) said he had spoken the truth (Bukhari {2}). This is the practice of the majority. Abu Hanifa allowed this combining only for one praying behind the Hajj imam, so many Hanafi groups pray each prayer at its own time in their tents. A pilgrim whose school counts them a resident of Makkah prays four rakahs each (see Mina's prayers); in the relied-upon Shafi'i view such a resident also prays each at its own time, since the combining is tied to travel. Prayed them separately, or at Asr time? Both prayers are valid and nothing is owed.

At sunset the Grand Mosque breaks its fast together. Charities and volunteers set out iftar in the mosque and its courtyards, commonly dates and Zamzam, and the spreads are cleared quickly so the rows can form for Maghrib. Spreads inside are run by permit holders with an approved food list and must not block walkways or emergency routes, so sit where staff direct you. The sunnah is to break the fast as soon as the sun has set (Bukhari {1}, {2}), with fresh dates, or dry dates, or a few sips of water (Abu Dawud {3}, graded hasan sahih by al-Albani).

Avoid pebbles from inside the basin, because they have already been thrown. The Hanbalis say a used pebble does not count (al-Mughni). The Shafi'is count it (al-Mughni). The Hanafis also dislike taking pebbles from beside the jamrah (al-Hidayah). A pebble from anywhere else counts for everyone.

Cannot afford a hady? The Quran's own alternative: fast three days during Hajj and seven days when you are home. Forgot to arrange it? It may be slaughtered until sunset on the {8}th according to Hanafis, Malikis and Hanbalis, or the {9}th according to many contemporary scholars (Shafi'is set no last day, though the {10}th is best); after that most scholars say it is still owed and must be made up. Changed into normal clothes before cutting? Put the ihram back on if you can and cut now. Whether a fidyah is owed differs: Shafi'is and Hanbalis excuse clothing worn forgetfully or unknowingly, but not cutting hair or nails; Hanafis require it regardless, and so do Malikis unless you had already stoned (for them the stoning alone opens the first tahallul); some Hanbalis and many contemporary scholars say nothing is owed for forgetting or not knowing (Bukhari {1}) — a fast of {2} days, feeding {3} poor, or a sheep (Quran {4}; the amounts are from Bukhari {5}). Shaved before the hady or before the rami? "No harm" (Bukhari {6}) for Shafi'is and Hanbalis; Hanafis: a dam; Malikis: a fidyah for shaving before the rami. Left Makkah without ever cutting? Cut as soon as you remember, wherever you are — until then intimacy stays forbidden. Hanafis and Malikis say a dam is owed; Shafi'is and Hanbalis say nothing is owed for the delay. Did not stay in Muzdalifah at all, or left before midnight without an excuse? The majority say a dam is owed (a sheep, slaughtered and given to the poor of the Haram); the Hajj is valid. Hanafis count the wajib as being there after Fajr, so leaving after midnight without excuse is also a dam for them. Those with a valid excuse (see the next step) owe nothing. Stuck in a bus queue and arrived only after Fajr? Scholars differ; most say nothing is owed if you did your best. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

Did them out of order? "No harm" (Bukhari {1}) — Shafi'is and Hanbalis say nothing is owed. Hanafis: a dam for shaving before the stoning, or (Qiran / Tamattu') for sacrificing before the stoning or shaving before the hady; Malikis: a fidyah for shaving before the stoning, and a dam for a tawaf al-ifadah done before it. Mention it to your group leader so the rest of the day is sequenced right, and ask a scholar if your group follows the Hanafi school.

Do not join the rush before sunset. When the disc has gone, follow your group to the buses or walk — the path is marked. Maghrib is not prayed on the road: when asked, the Prophet ﷺ said "the prayer is ahead of you" (Bukhari {1}). Keep the talbiyah going.
